angularDiameterSource: Radius 78.9 ± 7.4 solar radii from Moravveji et al. (2012), ApJ 747, 108, who combine the limb-darkened angular diameter 2.75 ± 0.01 mas of Aufdenberg et al. (2008) with the Hipparcos distance.
distanceSource: Inverse of the Hipparcos new-reduction parallax 3.78 ± 0.34 mas (van Leeuwen 2007) via SIMBAD
radiusSource: Radius: Radius 78.9 ± 7.4 solar radii from Moravveji et al. (2012), ApJ 747, 108, who combine the limb-darkened angular diameter 2.75 ± 0.01 mas of Aufdenberg et al. (2008) with the Hipparcos distance. Adopted 54,890,730 km, 78.9000 solar radii at 695700 km per solar radius. No gravitational parameter is adopted. presentationUp: the display axis (celestial north at the star) is up; no spin axis is adopted.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Effective temperature 12100 ± 150 K from Przybilla et al. 2010 (A&A 517, A38; https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/201014164), Table 1, HD 34085: a non-LTE spectroscopic analysis. The radius source, Moravveji et al. 2012, adopts this value in its Table 1.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius in the shared neutral gray; no picture of the photosphere is cast.
